title: International new-hire relocation & remote 90-day activation cookbook
body:
Purpose:
This working cookbook is a practical checklist and playbook for early-career international hires who are either relocating to a local office or joining fully remote. Focus is on reducing friction in the first 90 days, aligning manager expectations, and ensuring legal/relocation compliance.

Scope:
- Roles: new grads, interns, and entry-level ICs across engineering, product, and design.
- Locations: primary focus APAC->US/EU relocations and hires who remain remote outside primary regions.
- This doc covers pre-offer to day-90 activation; separate resource exists for senior/managerial relocation (link in linked_artifacts).

Quick notes (working):
- Budget bands currently: $6k–$12k relocation for early-career depending on region. Confirm FY26 budget line.
- Visa turnaround times: SE Asia -> US typical 4–10 weeks; Europe faster but finance hold required.
- Equipment: standard laptop + dongles + local power adapter + portable monitor for remote hires.

Pre-offer checklist (People Ops / Recruiter):
- Confirm role-level relocation eligibility and budget band. (Owner: recruiter)
- Check candidate citizenship/visa needs; flag to Legal/Immigration. (Owner: recruiter)
- Draft relocation clause in offer (template: GDrive:templates/relocation-agreement-v2).
- Estimate start date window accounting for visa/relocation (add buffer: +3 weeks).

Offer stage / acceptance tasks:
- Send relocation packet + FAQ (local housing tips, tax basics, sample lease).
- Assign onboarding buddy (same function, same timezone if possible).
- Create calendar placeholder for first 90 days: intro, manager 1:1s, role kickoff, and eval checkpoints.

Pre-start (2 weeks before start):
- IT: provision laptop order + tracking (tracker link to JIRA:HR-4821).
- Payroll: confirm local payroll/legal entity; set up contractor-to-employee conversion process if needed.
- Tax: send initial forms, tax residency questionnaire.
- Relocation vendor: confirm moving dates & approvals.
- Slack/email provisioning: create account user and add to team channels.

Day 0 / first 48 hours checklist:
- Welcome email + manager welcome video link.
- Buddy intro message; 30-minute coffee scheduled.
- Hardware check: confirm device delivered, accessories present, VPN access tested.
- Security onboarding (MFA, password manager invite).
- HR orientation (benefits overview, payroll setup).

Week 1 (orientation & small wins):
- Team intro + 1:1 with manager (30–45m): align on role, success signals, and early projects.
- Shadow sessions: schedule 3 short shadow blocks with teammates.
- Quick technical setup task: run local dev environment + run tests (owner: eng lead).
- Complete corporate compliance e-learning modules.

Weeks 2–4 (ramp):
- 30-day goals: contribute to a small bugfix / documentation improvement; present what was learned in team sync.
- Checkpoint: manager 30-day review (15m + written notes).
- Buddy-led orientation: internal tools walkthrough, codebase map, recurring team rituals.
- Relocation follow-up: ensure housing and stipend disbursement processed.

Month 2 (weeks 5–8):
- 60-day goals: deliver a scoped feature or owned component with code review.
- Cross-functional intro: schedule 1:1s with product and design partners.
- Career development: register for internal learning path (courses + mentorship).
- Manager 60-day review: calibrate trajectory and stretch areas.

Month 3 (weeks 9–12):
- 90-day goals: own a small-to-medium feature from design to deploy; demonstrate steady pull request cadence and clear communication.
- Formal 90-day review: manager + people-ops + mentor present; set 6-month objectives.
- Graduation checklist: badge, team rotation preferences, expanded access as needed.

Buddy & mentor program specifics:
- Buddy: near-peer (same level or +1), primarily social + day-to-day questions; meet 3x first two weeks, weekly through month 1, biweekly months 2–3.
- Mentor: senior IC, career coach for 6 months; monthly 1:1s and goal-setting.
- Feedback loop: buddies submit a short 30-day buddy report to people-ops (template: linked_artifacts).

Manager responsibilities (first 90 days):
- Create success criteria for 30/60/90 and share in writing within 48h of start.
- Weekly 1:1s first 6 weeks, then maintain cadence.
- Fast feedback: PR reviews within 48h for ramping hires.
- Escalate any blockers to people-ops within 72h.

Legal / Immigration notes:
- For visa-assisted hires, keep candidate updated weekly.
- Document copies: passport, offer acceptance, visa docs stored in secure HR folder (follow KMS policy).
- Tax residency reminders: send 30/60 day check-ins for forms.

Equipment & home office stipend:
- Standard kit: MacBook Pro 14" (or Windows equivalent), monitor, keyboard, mouse, USB-C dock, power adapter.
- Home office stipend: one-time $400 local currency-equivalent; receipts within 60 days.
- International shipping: use vendor where available; else ship from regional office.

Simple interview rubric (for hiring similar early-career international candidates) — one-page style:
- Criteria: problem solving (30%), communication & collaboration (25%), fundamentals (CS/role-specific) (30%), culture fit & ownership (15%).
- Score band: 1–4 (1: not meeting, 2: developing, 3: meets expectations, 4: exceeds).
- Passing threshold: aggregate >= 3.0 and no critical 1 in problem solving or communication.
- Sample questions per criterion:
  - Problem solving: "walk me through optimizing this simple algorithm" / whiteboard small challenge.
  - Communication: "explain a technical decision you made to a non-technical stakeholder."
  - Fundamentals: role-specific prompt (e.g., debugging logs, data structures).
  - Culture: "tell me about a time you owned a project end-to-end."
- Interview flow: Recruiter screen (30m) -> Two technical interviews (coding + system design-lite, 45m each) -> Team culture round (30m).
- Notes: allow extra time for non-native speakers and avoid idiomatic language in prompts.

Hiring plan (typical timeline for entry-level international role):
- Sourcing & initial outreach: 2–4 weeks.
- Recruiter screens: 1 week.
- Interview loop & decision: 2 weeks.
- Offer negotiation & acceptance: 1 week.
- Visa/relocation processing: 4–10 weeks (start planning earlier).
- Target start date buffer: 3–6 weeks after acceptance to allow logistics.

Measurement & success signals:
- Ramp metrics: first PR merged within 30 days, first owned story within 60 days, 90-day review rating >= meets expectations.
- Retention: 12-month retention target 85%+ for early-career hires.
- Candidate experience: NPS target: 60+ for relocation experience.

Unresolved / open questions:
- Confirm final FY26 relocation budget bands and approval path (Finance).
- Standardize local housing package vs. stipend — pilot or fixed policy?
- Are we centralizing vendor for APAC->US moves or using regionals?

Next steps (owners):
- People-ops: finalize relocation packet and FAQ (owner: Aisha).
- Legal: confirm visa timeline assumptions and policy language (owner: Priya).
- Eng hiring leads: adopt interview rubric and give feedback after 1 quarter (owner: Miguel).

Appendix: quick checklists (copyable)
- Offer packet checklist: offer letter, relocation clause, tentative start date, immigration contact card, equipment expectations.
- Day 0 checklist (copy for manager): manager welcome message, 1:1 scheduled, PR environment access verified, buddy introduced.

Notes to self: keep this doc concise; separate country-specific playbooks (India, Philippines, Brazil) into regional folders when we lock policies.

"This is a working doc — please leave comments inline and tag @Aisha for approvals."
